messages.subject: ggplot2 Legend Color (Manual Scale) Override
parts:
Hi!

Running the following:

library("ggplot2")
library("scales")

testdf <- data.frame(x=rnorm(100), y=rnorm(100), flag=c("flag")) p <-
ggplot(testdf, aes(x=x, y=y, color=flag)) + layer(geom="point") +
scale_color_manual("Flag", values=c(alpha("red", 1/5)))


generates a scatterplot where overlapping points cause an increase in
apparent alpha until at 5 points the apparent alpha becomes 1.

This is good.

The legend that is generated shows a dot with alpha @ .20 though.  I would
like the legend dot to be at maximum alpha.

From some online searching I found this:

guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1)

It makes sense but I do not set the alpha on the geom but rather on the
individual colors.  I do this because not every color I want to display
wants to have the same alpha value.

In reality I use:  scale_color_manual(“Title”, values=c(alpha(“black”,1/10),
“red”, alpha(“blue”, 1/5)))

I tried this:

p + guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(values = c("red"))))

thinking the matching the “values” from the scale_color_manual within the
override list would have some effect - but nothing changed.

Any ideas on the magic words to get the legend to show pure red while
maintaining the ability to have multiple colors with independent alphas?

Thanks!

David J.

messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 Legend Color (Manual Scale) Override
parts:
Hi:

Is this what you're looking for?

testdf <- data.frame(x=rnorm(100), y=rnorm(100),
                     flag = factor(sample(1:3, 100, replace = TRUE)))

scale_color_manual("Title", values = c(alpha("black", 0.1), "red",
                                             alpha("blue", 0.2)))
p + guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1)))

Also note that I changed 1/10 and 1/5 to their decimal equivalents because an error message re 'unexpected input' kept arising until I changed it.

See p. 7 of the 0.9.0 transition guide for an example of this behavior, as well as the examples on the guide_legend() help page:
http://cloud.github.com/downloads/hadley/ggplot2/guide-col.pdf

Dennis
